stories.title: Susan Thomas and the Dog Bite
stories.description: Amit recounts how Susan Thomas was bitten by a dog in Kerala. Contrary to the typical Indian experience, she went to a government clinic where a competent doctor asked the right questions (is the dog observed?) and prescribed antiseptic instead of unnecessary rabies shots. This highlights the superior state capacity and local governance in Kerala.

stories.title: Baba and the Pope
stories.description: Ajay tells a joke about a man named Baba who claims to know everyone. After proving it with Trump and Biden, he appears on the Vatican balcony with the Pope, prompting a spectator to ask, 'Who's that guy with Baba?'

stories.title: The Monkey and the Two Cats
stories.description: Ajay uses the fable of the monkey mediating a dispute between two cats over bread (and eating it all himself) to explain the vertical devolution problem: the Union government keeping the lion's share of resources.

stories.title: Dutch Tanks and the German Army
stories.description: Amit explains how the Netherlands integrated its tank battalions into the German army because maintaining a small independent force was inefficient. This illustrates the principle of assigning functions to the appropriate scale (European Union logic).

recommendations.item: The Death and Life of Great American Cities
recommendations.comment: Jane Jacobs' masterpiece on organic city growth, recommended by Amit.
Robert Caro's biography of Robert Moses, contrasting with Jane Jacobs' philosophy.
Edward Glaeser's book on the importance of cities.
Vijay Kelkar and Ajay Shah's book discussing the architecture of the Indian state.
Nilakantan RS's book highlighting the disparities between Southern and Northern Indian states.
Albert O. Hirschman's classic on responses to decline in firms, organizations, and states.

core_ideas.description: The idea that functions should be performed at the lowest effective level of government. Mosquito control belongs to the city; currency belongs to the nation.
India's immense diversity (economic, cultural, health) means a centralized 'one-size-fits-all' approach fails. Kerala needs diabetes management, while UP needs malnutrition solutions.
Cities and villages face different governance challenges. Cities have economies of scale for services; villages often don't. Treating them identically (73rd/74th amendments) is a flaw.
Migration allows citizens to 'vote with their feet' (Exit), moving to better-governed areas. This should be celebrated as it creates competition between states and improves lives.
The critical issue of how much tax revenue the Union government shares with states, which is often insufficient compared to what the Union retains.
A true republic requires checks and balances. Currently, power is too concentrated in the PMO (Union) and CMs (States), leading to authoritarian tendencies.
